newsitem.title: ISRAEL: First Int'l Bank Q2 EPS 10.59 shekels.
newsitem.headline: First Int'l Bank Q2 EPS 10.59 shekels.

text.p: First International Bank of Israel on Tuesday reported a 24 percent increase in second-quarter net earnings to 53.13 million shekels, or 10.59 shekels a share, compared with a year earlier.

For the first half, net earnings rose 22.6 percent to 100.19 million shekels, boosting annualised net return on equity to 9.8 percent. That compared with 8.3 percent a year earlier and 9.2 percent for all of 1996.
First International, one of Israel's five largest banks, attributed the increase in first-half net to increased lending and capital market activity.
Income from financial operations rose 8.3 percent to 397.7 million shekels, while operating income was up 16.3 percent to 257.3 million shekels.
These factors offset narrower financial margins, a 22.7 percent rise in the debt provision to 38.37 million shekels and a 4.2 million shekel charge for inflationary accounting, the bank said.

Operating expenses were 7.3 percent higher in the period to 405.5 million shekels. "The increase was mainly attributed to a rise in the number of employees as a direct result of the bank's business development," First International said.

It said shareholders' equity grew to 2.2 billion shekels as of June 30, a rise of 3.3 percent from the end of 1996. Total assets amounted to 34.8 billion shekels at the end of the quarter, compared with 29.5 billion shekels a year earlier and 31.7 billion shekels at the end of 1996.

The bank noted that new banking directives required it to discount credit from Treasury sources not at the bank's risk as well as deposits earmarked for financing this credit. Balance sheet data for 1996 was adjusted retroactively to reflect the changes.

Credit to the public was up 14.3 percent at the end of the quarter compared with a year earlier to 23.7 billion shekels, while deposits from the public reached 29.1 billion shekels, a rise of 17.6 percent on the year.
